name: USG Hydrocal White gypsum cement (cast into the wall)
note: USG: use consistency 45 lb water per 100 lb, wet density 110 lb/ft3, dry density 90 lb/ft3. Powder to buy per volume derived: wet density times 100/145. A hard, heavy cast with high inner damping between two printed walls (the 'dental plaster' DIY build).

source.title: USG Industrial Plasters and Gypsum Cement, product comparison (Freeman Supply copy)

loss_factor_source.title: Tom Irvine, Damping Properties of Materials, Revision D (Vibrationdata, 2010-07-02), Table 7
loss_factor_source.note: Table 7 gives 'Plaster' a loss factor of 0.02 to 0.05; the record holds the middle.

youngs_source.title: USG Hydrocal FGR 95 Gypsum Cement data sheet, IG1960 rev. 12-16
youngs_source.note: USG publishes no stiffness for Hydrocal White. Derived: FGR 95's modulus of elasticity in flexure, 14.5 to 15.2 GPa (middle 14.85) at 1650 to 1794 kg/m3 (middle 1722), scaled to Hydrocal White's dry density, 1442 kg/m3, by the square of the density ratio (the usual law for a porous solid): 10.41 GPa. FGR 95 is made for glass-fibre casts, so its figure may include fibre; treat this as uncertain by a factor of two.
